svg.text: THE NESTED HIERARCHY — SENTENCE › CLAUSE › PHRASE
It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.
It was a bright cold day in April
▾ left clause decomposes into clause elements (2.6) — phrases fill each slot
▾ the NP decomposes into word classes (§4)
Orwell, "1984" (1.2). Bold = the item each level's decomposition targets. The right-hand clause decomposes the same way.
"in April" is read here as a clause-level adverbial (2.6); it may alternatively be analysed as a postmodifier inside the NP "a bright cold day in April" (3.1).

text.tspan: Labelled bracketing (1.2), same sentence, compact notation:
[S [NP It] [VP [V was] [NP a bright cold day] [PP in April]]]

svg.text: Simple — one independent clause (1.1) ○ "Call me Ishmael." (Melville)
Complex — independent + one or more dependent clauses (1.3)
Declarative — makes a statement or opinion
Tag question — reversed-polarity tag repeats aux + pronoun
Dependent — attaches to an independent clause (2.2)
Adverbial — modifies V/Adj/Adv: time, reason, condition… (2.4)
Non-finite — verb untensed, subject usu. unexpressed (2.7)
to-infin. "to leave tomorrow" · bare infin. "him sing"
DEPENDENCY VIEW — what modifies what (contrast the constituency tree, Block 1) · McGuffey (2.6)
Adjunct modifies the verb, inside the clause ("sang beautifully"); disjunct modifies the whole clause, states stance — frontable/parenthesisable is the diagnostic ("Frankly, she was wrong") (2.6)
§3 — the unit that fills a clause element
Every phrase has a head (names its type); modifiers are optional/removable ("the big dog"); complements are required ("relies on her team") (§3)
Modal › Perfect (have) › Progressive (be+-ing) › Passive (be+-en) › Main verb
She may have been being interviewed.
PP — prep + object; complement or adjunct (3.3)
= same material as the non-finite clauses at 2.7, seen at phrase level.
